memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "...then the Lord your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you and gather you again from all the nations where he scattered you. Even if you have been banished to the most distant land under the heavens, from there the Lord your God will gather you and bring you back." — Deut 30:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When His people turn back, God promises to act. He will restore, have compassion, and gather them home — even from "the most distant land under the heavens." No place is too far, no situation too hopeless for God to reach and restore. The same God who scattered in discipline promised to gather in mercy. His compassion always has the last word.

Notice that word "compassion." God's gathering of His people is not grudging or reluctant. It flows from His deep, tender love. He does not merely tolerate the return of His people; He has compassion on them. His heart moves toward them with mercy.

This was fulfilled in part when God brought Israel back from exile, keeping His word across the generations. But it points to something even greater. Jesus described Himself as the Good Shepherd who goes after the lost and gathers His scattered sheep, willing to bring in even those far off (John 10:16). Through Christ, God gathers people "from every nation, tribe, people and language" into His family (Rev 7:9).

So if you feel scattered, distant, or far from where you should be, take heart. There is no "distant land" beyond the reach of God's gathering compassion. The Good Shepherd knows how to find and bring home every one of His own. Whatever exile you feel yourself in, His mercy can reach you there and bring you back.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God's compassion can reach me wherever I am?
2. How does the image of God "gathering" His people comfort me?
3. Is there a "distant land" in my life I need God to bring me back from?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Compassionate God, no place is too far for Your mercy to reach. Thank You that You gather Your scattered people with tender love. Bring me home to Your heart, wherever I have strayed. Amen.
